content: 1. A study published in Public Health Nutrition in 2006 (Volume 9, Issue 8, Pages 968–974) explored health factors related to malnutrition in older adults. 2. The Mini Nutritional Assessment International Group conducted a multinational study using the Mini Nutritional Assessment tool to evaluate malnutrition in older adults. This research was published in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society in 2010 (Volume 58, Issue 9, Pages 1734–1738). 3. Keller HH, Ostbye T, and Goy R demonstrated that nutritional risk is a predictor of quality of life in elderly Canadians living in the community. Their findings were published in the Journal of Gerontology: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences in 2004 (Volume 59, Pages 68–74). 4. Keller H, Beck AM, and Namasivayam A, as part of the International Dining in Nursing Home Experts (I-DINE) Consortium, proposed a research agenda to improve food and fluid intake among older adults in long-term care. This was published in the Journal of the American Medical Directors Association in 2015 (Volume 16, Issue 2, Pages 93–100). 5. Kwon J, Yoshida Y, Yoshida H, Kim H, Suzuki T, and Lee Y conducted a randomized controlled trial to assess the effects of combined physical training and nutritional intervention on physical performance and health-related quality of life in prefrail older women living in the community. Their findings were published in the Journal of the American Medical Directors Association. 6. Liu W, Galik E, Boltz M, Nahm ES, and Resnick B performed a systematic review on optimizing eating performance in older adults with dementia living in long-term care. This was published in Worldviews on Evidence-Based Nursing in 2015 (Volume 12, Issue 4, Pages 228–235). 7. Liu HY, Tseng MY, Li HJ, Wu CC, Cheng HS, Yang CT, and colleagues demonstrated that comprehensive care improves physical recovery in elderly Taiwanese patients with hip fractures and poor nutritional status. This study was published in the Journal of the American Medical Directors Association in 2014 (Volume 15, Issue 6, Pages 416–422). 8. Locher JL, Robinson CO, Roth DL, Ritchie CS, and Burgio KL investigated the effect of social presence on caloric intake in homebound older adults. Their findings were published in the Journal of Gerontology: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences in 2005 (Volume 60, Issue 11, Pages 1475–1478). 9. Locher JL, Roth DL, Ritchie CS, Cox K, Sawyer P, Bodner EV, and Allman RM examined the relationship between body mass index, weight loss, and mortality in community-dwelling older adults. This study was published in the Journal of Gerontology: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences in 2007 (Volume 62, Issue 12, Pages 1389–1392). 10. Locher JL, Vickers KS, Buys DR, Ellis A, Lawrence JC, Newton LE, and colleagues conducted a randomized controlled trial of a theoretically-based behavioral nutrition intervention for community elders. Lessons from this study were published in the Journal of the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics in 2013 (Volume 113, Issue 12, Pages 1675–1682). 11. Mahadevan M, Hartwell HJ, Feldman CH, Ruzsilla JA, and Raines ER explored the mealtime experiences of elderly individuals in assisted living. Their findings were published in the Journal of Human Nutrition and Dietetics in 2014 (Volume 27, Issue 2, Pages 152–161). 12. Margetts BM, Thompson RL, Elia M, and Jackson AA reported that the prevalence of undernutrition risk is associated with poor health status in older adults in the UK. This study was published in the European Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2003 (Volume 57, Pages 69–74). 13. Milne AC, Potter J, Vivanti A, and Avenell A conducted a Cochrane systematic review on protein and energy supplementation in elderly individuals at risk of malnutrition. This review was published in 2009 (Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, Issue 2, Article CD003288). 14. Payette H evaluated the efficacy of nutritional interventions in free-living frail elderly individuals. This research was published in the American Journal of Clinical Nutrition in 2002 (Volume 75, Supplement 2, Page 340S). 15. Pivi GA, da Silva RV, Juliano Y, Novo NF, Okamoto IH, Brant CQ, and colleagues conducted a prospective study on nutrition education and oral nutritional supplementation in patients with Alzheimer’s disease. This study was published in Nutrition Journal in 2011 (Volume 10, Article 98). 16. Ramic E, Pranjic N, Batic-Mujanovic O, Karic E, Alibasic E, and Alic A examined the impact of loneliness on malnutrition in the elderly population. Their findings were published in Medical Archives in 2011 (Volume 65, Issue 2, Pages 92–95). 17. Rosendahl E, Lindelof N, Littbrand H, Yifter-Lindgren E, Lundin-Olsson L, Haglin L, and colleagues conducted a randomized controlled trial on a high-intensity functional exercise program combined with protein-enriched energy supplements for older adults dependent on daily living activities. This study was published in the Australian Journal of Physiotherapy in 2006 (Volume 52, Issue 2, Pages 105–113). 18. Shahar DR, Schultz R, Shahar A, and Wing RR investigated the effects of widowhood on weight change, dietary intake, and eating behavior in the elderly population. Their findings were published in Journal of Aging and Health in 2001 (Volume 13, Issue 2, Pages 186–199). 19. Sharkey JR, Branch LG, Giuliani C, Zohoori N, and Haines PS identified nutrient intake and body mass index as predictors of the severity of disability in activities of daily living over one year in homebound older adults. This study was published in the Journal of Nutrition, Health, and Aging in 2004 (Volume 8, Issue 3, Pages 131–139). 20. Vedantam A, Subramanian V, Vijay Rao N, and John KR reported on the prevalence and risk factors of malnutrition in free-living elderly individuals in rural South India. This study was published in Public Health Nutrition in 2010 (Volume 13, Issue 9, Pages 1328–1332). 21. Vucea V, Keller HH, and Ducak K reviewed interventions aimed at improving mealtime experiences in long-term care settings. Their findings were published in the Journal of Nutrition in Gerontology and Geriatrics in 2014 (Volume 33, Issue 4, Pages 249–324). 22. Wouters-Wesseling W, Wagenaar LW, Rozendaal M, Deijen JB, de Groot LC, Bindels JG, and colleagues investigated the effect of an enriched drink on cognitive function in frail elderly individuals. This study was published in the Journal of Gerontology: Biological Sciences and Medical Sciences in 2005 (Volume 60, Issue 2, Pages 265–270).
